definition.lead: This page tracks AI in chemistry where it has actually delivered: real molecules, real materials and real decisions, not just promises.
definition.body: Each use case is judged by evidence: was the prediction tested in the lab, did it beat existing methods, and did it change what chemists do? From antibiotic discovery to protein design and materials screening, the record is growing fast, along with lessons from failures.

timeline.title: A first win
timeline.text: Deep learning wins Merck's molecular activity challenge.
timeline.why: Signalled deep learning's potential in chemistry.

timeline.title: Molecules in weeks
timeline.text: Insilico Medicine reports kinase inhibitors designed with generative AI, made and tested in weeks.

timeline.title: Halicin
timeline.text: A deep learning screen at MIT identifies halicin as an antibacterial candidate.
timeline.why: AI found a structurally unusual antibiotic.

timeline.title: AlphaFold structures released
timeline.text: Predicted structures for the human proteome and more become freely available.

timeline.title: 200 million structures
timeline.text: The AlphaFold database expands to over 200 million predictions.

timeline.title: Millions of predicted crystals
timeline.text: DeepMind's GNoME reports 2.2 million new predicted crystal structures; how many are truly new is debated.
timeline.why: AI scaled materials screening, and raised questions about validation.

timeline.title: Nobel Prize
timeline.text: Baker, Hassabis and Jumper share the Chemistry prize for protein design and structure prediction.
timeline.why: AI tools recognized at the highest level.

quiz.q: What is the strongest evidence for an AI chemistry claim?
options: Prospective lab validation of new predictions
High accuracy on the training data
A press release
A large model size
quiz.explain: Predict first, then test what nobody had tested before.

options: A deep learning model screened molecules for antibacterial activity
A random screen of soil bacteria found it by luck
It was designed atom by atom by a quantum chemistry program
Chemists modified an existing antibiotic step by step
quiz.explain: Then it was tested against real bacteria.

quiz.q: A retrospective benchmark differs from a prospective study because…
options: It tests on already-known data, while a prospective study predicts and then tests new cases
It always gives more reliable results than a prospective study
It requires new lab experiments for every prediction
It is run in the lab before any model is trained
quiz.explain: Retrospective scores can be inflated by hidden overlaps.

quiz.q: Why do AI models often fail on genuinely new chemistry?
options: The training data lacks similar examples (out of distribution)
Their hardware is too slow for complex molecules
Chemistry has no consistent rules for a model to learn
Larger models always memorize every possible molecule
quiz.explain: Models interpolate well and extrapolate poorly.

options: Finds good conditions in fewer experiments
Needs thousands of runs
Works without any data
Only works for polymers
quiz.explain: It models uncertainty to choose informative experiments.

options: Millions of predicted new inorganic crystal structures
A new broad-spectrum antibiotic for resistant bacteria
The structures of every protein in the human body
A battery cathode that doubled energy density
quiz.explain: Experts have since debated how many are novel and useful.

quiz.q: What did Insilico Medicine's 2019 study show?
options: Generative AI designed kinase inhibitors that were made and tested within weeks
AI could replace clinical trials for new kinase drugs
A deep learning model rediscovered penicillin from text
Robots alone completed a full drug approval process
quiz.explain: A proof of speed, not yet of a medicine.

options: Negative results are rarely published, so data is skewed toward successes
Journals refuse to publish any paper that uses machine learning
Published data is too accurate for models to learn from
Successful experiments are usually hidden in patents only
Experts review and steer AI suggestions
A human inside the robot
Humans are removed
Only humans make decisions
quiz.explain: Combines model speed with expert judgement.

quiz.q: A fair test of a new AI method compares it against…
options: Strong non-AI methods and simple baseline models
Only previous versions of the same AI model
Results reported in the AI method's own press release
Random guessing, since that is the lowest bar
quiz.explain: Many claims shrink against good baselines.

quiz.q: How many predicted structures does the AlphaFold database hold?
options: Over 200 million
About 1,000
About 100,000
Exactly 20,000

quiz.q: What does data leakage do to reported performance?
options: Inflates it
Lowers it
Has no effect
Makes it random
